audit_findings.title: UniFirst closing would invalidate both the earnings numerator and share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $5.5 billion transaction value; approximately $2.8 billion expected additional debt; consideration also includes 0.7720 CTAS share per UniFirst share
audit_findings.mechanism: A completed acquisition changes OE, prospective growth, fully diluted shares, cash, debt and interest expense in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the Transaction, UniFirst shareholders will receive the merger consideration, which consists of (i) $155.00 in cash and (ii) 0.7720 of validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable shares of Cintas common stock (with, if applicable, cash in lieu of fractional shares), in each case without interest and subject to any required tax withholding, and each applicable holder of such shares of UniFirst stock will cease to have any rights with respect thereto, except the right to receive the applicable merger consideration.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved current-date fact, not a demonstrated valuation error. The July 29 filing establishes that the transaction was pending and expected to close in the second half of 2026, but it does not establish its status on September 4. Closing would change nearly every principal valuation input and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain transaction-status evidence effective September 4, 2026. If closed, rerun with post-closing earnings, consideration shares, cash outflow, financing, interest, integration costs and balance-sheet amounts; if still pending, retain the AS_FILED warning.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash includes a declared dividend liability belonging to earlier record-date holders
audit_findings.magnitude: $180.7 million, equal to $0.44 per valuation share and 62.5% of the $289.018 million cash bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds May 31 cash without deducting the accrued dividend that was paid June 15 to May 15 record-date holders.
audit_findings.evidence: The dividends declared on April 14, 2026 and April 8, 2025, were included in current accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets at May 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date-matching error because the September valuation and June 30 denominator represent holders who did not own the claim to the accrued dividend. Correcting it reduces every scenario by about $0.44 per share, approximately 0.5% of the $84.83 base value, and cannot bridge the gap between the $201.05 price and the $99.80 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Deduct $180.7 million from bridge cash or replace both cash and relevant liabilities with a consistent post-payment balance-sheet date.

audit_findings.title: Retained historical interest may not represent the imminent refinancing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.4 billion of principal matures over the next two fiscal years; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Refinancing rates change interest expense retained within equity-level OE and therefore affect forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Maturities of debt during each of the next five fiscal years are $ 1,000.0 million, $ 400.0 million, $ 0.0 million, $ 0.0 million and $ 0.0 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The maturities are demonstrated, but a valuation error is not: the record does not establish the refinancing instruments, rates, repayment amounts or timing. Refinancing above the existing 3.70% and 4.20% coupons would reduce value, while repayment or cheaper refinancing could increase it. The possible effect is therefore real but its materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Build a debt schedule using documented refinancing or repayment plans and rerun OE with scenario-specific post-tax interest expense for the $1.0 billion and $400 million maturities.

audit_findings.title: Not all added cash is available to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $37.2 million, equal to $0.09 per valuation share and 12.9% of bridge cash
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted collateral is included in the cash add-on even though it is not presently distributable to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: At May 31, 2026 and 2025, cash and cash equivalents includes $ 37.2 million and $ 35.8 million, respectively, of restricted cash used as collateral associated with our insurance reserve.
audit_findings.explanation: The restriction is filed and the bridge includes the full cash balance, so the overstatement is demonstrated unless the associated obligation is separately netted. Removing $37.2 million reduces value by about $0.09 per share, roughly 0.1% of base value, and cannot affect the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Exclude $37.2 million from bridge cash unless a documented, consistently treated insurance obligation releases or offsets the collateral.

audit_findings.title: A transaction-specific one-off appears retained in the stand-alone anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.1 million pretax, 0.81% of the $1,986.9 million anchor; full pretax sensitivity is approximately $0.46-$0.80 per share across the reported scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining a nonrecurring acquisition expense lowers the latest-year OE anchor and all forecast and terminal cash flows derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the Transaction with UniFirst, the Company incurred $16.1 million in transaction expenses in fiscal 2026 which relate primarily to legal and professional services, regulatory fees and financing fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The $16.1 million charge is filed, including $15.1 million in SG&A and $1.0 million in interest expense. Its retention is conservative for a stand-alone perimeter, although the exact after-tax normalization requires confirmation. Even the deliberately generous sensitivity of adding back the entire pretax amount increases the bull value by only about $0.80 per share and cannot alter the conclusion relative to the $201.05 price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the charge through the FY2026 OE calculation and, for a stand-alone rerun, add back only its documented after-tax nonrecurring portion; supersede this treatment with a full transaction model if UniFirst closed.

audit_findings.title: Unvested restricted awards may be counted twice in the denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: 1.878501 million shares, 0.45% of the 413.553511 million denominator; removal would raise reported values to approximately $58.12, $85.22 and $100.25 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A duplicated participating-share count enlarges the fully diluted denominator and depresses value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The recipient of restricted stock awards will have all rights of a shareholder of Cintas, including the right to vote and the right to receive cash dividends during the vesting period.
audit_findings.explanation: Double counting is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated error, because the transfer-agent count has not been reconciled to the award ledger. Its maximum identified effect is nevertheless bounded: removing all 1.878501 million awards raises the bull value by only about $0.45 per share and leaves it far below the $201.05 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 30 shares outstanding with the restricted-award ledger and remove the 1.878501 million increment if those issued participating shares are already included.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.8 million in FY2025, stated as 5.4% of filed D&A and equal to 1.35% of the FY2026 anchor as a scale comparison
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE, potentially affecting historical trend and forecast cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2025 $26.8m (5.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative omission is demonstrated, but eligibility for an add-back is unresolved; therefore no valuation error is established. The identified residual relates to FY2025, while the valuation anchor is the lower, capped FY2026 actual, so no direct anchor increase is demonstrated. Even treating the entire $26.8 million as a recurring add-back would imply only about $0.77-$1.34 per share across the reported scenarios and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the residual D&A component schedule and rerun only amounts supported as eligible non-economic add-backs, with particular attention to whether a comparable FY2026 residual exists.
